articles.title: Ivy League football team gets ruthlessly mocked after losing game in dumbest way possible
articles.summary: The University of Pennsylvania's botched clock management against Columbia left a 52-yard field goal woefully short, ending an Ivy League thriller in chaos.
articles.body: We had an Ivy League thriller during Friday night's three-pack college football weekend appetizer, with the University of Pennsylvania and Columbia going down to the wire in Philadelphia. That's right. Penn and Columbia. While the rest of the country flipped between Memphis, App State and Purdue, I was locked in the Ivy League battle of the year. It's called GRINDING, folks. Look it up. HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL Anyway, I'm glad I was, because this one had it all. Big moments. Big comebacks. Big plays. And, of course, a finish that left me utterly speechless on multiple different levels. Before we dive into the Xs and Os, take a look: Feel like an Ivy League school should've thought this through Amazing. You just don't expect that sort of foolishness out of an Ivy League roster, right? Sure, there are other programs where you wouldn't be surprised to see this level of idiocy (I won't name names), but not Penn. Not the IVY LEAGUE. These are supposed to be the smartest dudes on the planet, and they can't run a simple fire drill with the clock ticking down? Get on the ball and SPIKE it! Why are they rushing their field goal kicker out there? There was plenty of time. He caught it was 10 seconds to go. The clock stops on a first down in college football when its under two minutes to go in a half. HARVARD FOOTBALL OUTSMARTS COLGATE ON HAIL MARY ATTEMPT TO WIN GAME IN FINAL SECONDS So the clock was stopped. There was plenty of time of left. And they instead opted to sprint the field goal unit onto the field, and have the kicker quickly try a 52-yard field goal? Clearly, the kicker had no idea what was happening, by the way. None. That's why he was the last one onto the field. He came sprinting into the camera with four seconds left, barely lined up (he looked too close), and then came up woefully short with the kick. Game over. Columbia wins. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Amazing. We've seen a lot of dumb football over the past week, mostly out of the NFL. You had Nick Sirianni doing dumb things across the pond with the ill-fated kickoff, and then Jayden Daniels and the Commanders running what just may be the dumbest play of all time in overtime against the Giants. I won't put this disaster by Penn on that level, but it's up there. A quick spike of the ball, and maybe one more pass play to try and gain a free 3-4 yards would've put the kicker in a much better spot. Duh. He probably drills it if that happens. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Instead, we got ... whatever that was. I think we all expected better out of an Ivy League school.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Injury Update, Latest Rumors on WR's Status for Patriots' Game vs. Jets
articles.summary: New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown returned to practice this week, after being on injured reserve with an ankle injury, and reportedly is expected to play Sunday's matchup against the New York Jets.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown returned to practice this week, after being on injured reserve with an ankle injury, and reportedly is expected to play Sunday's matchup against the New York Jets.

Brown updated reporters on his status on Thursday:

"I feel pretty good," Brown said. "It's one step at a time with me, each and every day, just trying to increase my [workload], and just see how I respond each and every day. But I feel good, on the grass, practicing, working on the sides a little more."

"He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple of days," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Wednesday. "I think it's difficult sometimes to stay engaged, but I think his routine was really good, and his ability to be around the guys in the meetings and then also focus on his rehab and treat everything as a pro."

Brown, 29, was New England's major offseason acquisition, coming over in an offseason trade from the Philadelphia Eagles. But he suffered a high-ankle sprain in the team's Week 1 loss against the Seattle Seahawks and his 21-day practice window was opened this week.

Getting back the three-time Pro Bowler and one-time Super Bowl champion will obviously boost an offense that was already starting to find its groove again in recent weeks, although the timeline for Brown's return remains uncertain.

Another offseason addition, Romeo Doubs, has led the passing attack in Brown's absence. He's caught 13 passes for 219 yards and two scores. Drake Maye has also relied on Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and tight end Hunter Henry, and the Patriots have run the ball well.

But Brown provides a downfield threat and is one of the best contested-catch weapons in football. Upon his return, he'll immediately be the top priority in the passing game and should create opportunities for his teammates as well.

"I think you see it in the NBA," Maye told reporters. "It's probably the closest thing that I can think of. When they start doubling the best player once they get past half court, then they're just leaving a corner 3 open or leaving a guy open for a dunk. So, it's kind of like playing receiver and with a guy like that—we've got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it's going to be tough on defenses."

articles.title: New Shedeur Sanders Trade Rumors Leak After Browns QB Hires Travis Hunter's Agent
articles.summary: Even though Shedeur Sanders recently hired an agent for the first time in his NFL career after previously representing himself, there's nothing to indicate he is leaving the Cleveland Browns imminently.
articles.body:
Even though Shedeur Sanders recently hired an agent for the first time in his NFL career after previously representing himself, there's nothing to indicate he is leaving the Cleveland Browns imminently.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , citing discussions with people around the league and Browns officials, it would be a surprise if Sanders were to be moved prior to the trade deadline.

Sanders' new agent, Adie von Gontard of Young Money APAA Sports, also represents Travis Hunter. Sanders and Hunter were teammates for three seasons in college.

A fifth-round pick in the 2025 draft, Sanders rookie contract runs through the 2028 season. He will become extension eligible after the 2027 campaign.

Cleveland's quarterback situation has quieted down somewhat because Deshaun Watson has had moments when he has looked okay. His 268 passing yards in a Week 4 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers were his most in a game since Sept. 24, 2023.

Last week was a significant step back for Watson, who finished 15-of-33 for 155 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in a 17-12 loss to the New York Jets.

The Browns being 3-2 so far has also taken some pressure off head coach Todd Monken.

Sanders' lone appearance so far this season was in Week 3 when he threw one pass in a win over the Carolina Panthers after Watson took a hard hit on the previous play.

One reason the Browns might not be looking to trade Sanders right now, according to Jones, is general manager Andrew Berry has "great affection" for the second-year quarterback.

Sanders started seven games as a rookie, leading the Browns to a 3-4 record. He threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight appearances last season.

articles.title: New Rumors on Bo Nix After Ryan Fitzpatrick Ripped Broncos QB in Viral Video After Win vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: Despite Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix's poor play during Thursday night's 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks, and former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick's scathing evaluation of his performance, Nix is reportedly still looked at highly within the Broncos organization.
articles.body:
Despite Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix's poor play during Thursday night's 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks, and former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick's scathing evaluation of his performance, Nix is reportedly still looked at highly within the Broncos organization.

According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, "Nobody in the Broncos' building is more competitive than Bo Nix. He's a hard worker. Teammates love him."

Pelissero relayed that information after Fitzpatrick, who is an analyst for the NFL on Prime Video, blasted Nix on Thursday night:

Among other things, Fitzpatrick said, "Bo Nix is not playing competitively. It's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing quarterback right now."

The 26-year-old Nix exceeded expectations over his first two NFL seasons, taking the Broncos to the playoffs twice, including the AFC Championship Game last season, and throwing for a total of 7,706 yards, 54 touchdowns and 23 interceptions, while also rushing for 786 yards and nine scores.

Although the Broncos have persevered against a tough schedule so far this season to get off to a 4-2 start, there is no doubt that Nix has regressed compared to his first two campaigns.

In addition to completing a career-low 60.3 percent of his passes, Nix has thrown for just 1,049 yards, six touchdowns and three picks through six games.

Per Doug Clawson of CBS Sports, Nix is currently having the most conservative start to a season by a quarterback over the past two decades in terms of air yards per attempt:

That conservatism was on full display Thursday, as Nix went 17-of-27 for 107 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions.

As seen in the NFL Next Gen Stats passing chart from Thursday's game, Nix did not complete a pass of 10 yards or more down the field, and seven of his completions occurred behind the line of scrimmage:

He was aided by an interception thrown by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold in overtime, which essentially put the Broncos in field goal range and allowed them to win the game.

Nix has never been one to consistently attack defenses down the field, averaging 6.7 yards per attempt as a rookie and 6.4 yards per attempt last season.

However, he is sitting at just 5.6 yards per attempt so far this season, which is surprising given that the Broncos upgraded their receiving corps during the offseason by acquiring Jaylen Waddle from the Miami Dolphins.

It should be noted that Nix has dealt with some turmoil in the coaching ranks, as offensive coordinator Davis Webb began the season as the offensive play-caller before getting supplanted by head coach Sean Payton.

Payton called the plays over Nix's first two seasons, and although that familiarity didn't seem to help much on Thursday, perhaps that will change as time goes on.

articles.title: Texans 'Aware' How Marvin Harrison Jr.'s 'Effort' Looked on Tape, New NFL Rumors Reveal After Trade
articles.summary: The Houston Texans aren't concerned about Marvin Harrison Jr.'s play during his time with the Arizona Cardinals after they gave up a second-round pick to acquire the veteran wide receiver.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans aren't concerned about Marvin Harrison Jr.'s play during his time with the Arizona Cardinals after they gave up a second-round pick to acquire the veteran wide receiver.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Texans are "aware" of the "lack of effort" that showed up on Harrison's tape at times during his time in Arizona and have confidence that won't carry over in part because he is because he gets to play with his former Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud:

"The Texans are aware of what Harrison's tape in Arizona looked like. And though he's been with the team for less than a week, there have been no signs within the organization that the lack of effort seen on tape has traveled with him to Houston (or, for that matter, London, where the Texans will play the Jaguars on Sunday).

"The flow of the game will likely dictate Harrison's snaps, but I'm told he has picked things up well and will do more as the year goes along. What will be interesting to see is how he adapts to playing opposite the X receiver, a position Nico Collins holds.

"'We're hoping that because of the dynamic with his college quarterback and a change of scenery, it will unlock him,' one team source says."

Harrison was regarded as one of the best receiver prospects in recent memory going into the 2024 NFL draft. He had an outstanding two-year run at Ohio State with 144 receptions for 2,474 yards and 28 touchdowns in 25 games from 2022 to '23.

B/R's NFL scouting department described Harrison as a "slam-dunk prospect" and cited A.J. Green as a comparison for his style of play.

The Cardinals made Harrison the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 draft. He was the highest-drafted wide receiver for the franchise since Larry Fitzgerald was selected third overall in 2004.

Harrison had a solid rookie season with 885 yards and eight touchdowns in 17 games, but things have fallen off dramatically since then. He has 693 yards and four touchdowns in 16 games since the start of the 2025 season.

There have been clips posted from games this season that appear to show Harrison not going at full speed, though Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur disagreed with the notion he wasn't playing hard.

It seems clear based on the trade package that the Texans believe a change of scenery and playing with a quarterback Harrison has familiarity with can turn things around. They gave up a 2027 second-round pick to acquire him from Arizona.

Houston desperately needed help at wide receiver with Jayden Higgins out for the season and Tank Dell still on injured reserve.

Nico Collins has missed time already due to a hamstring injury, though he has looked fine with 174 yards and two touchdowns in two games since returning.

The combination of Stroud at quarterback and Collins being the No. 1 option in the offense should ease some of the pressure on Harrison. He's only 24 and has one more guaranteed year on his rookie contract, so the upside for a Texans team trying to get back on track amid a 1-4 start makes it worth the risk for them.

Harrison will make his Texans debut on Sunday when they play the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium in London, England.

articles.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts ruled out for Week 6 after blood clot found in his leg, not expected to go on IR
articles.summary: If Hurts were to be placed on IR he would miss at least four weeks.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are not planning on placing quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after a superficial blood clot was discovered in his leg .

According to Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , the Eagles believe the blood clot is treatable and do not feel the need to shut Hurts down for at least four weeks with an IR stint. Both parties are gathering more information and seeking out other medical opinions.

Hurts has already been ruled out for this week's game against the Carolina Panthers.

The Eagles released a statement Thursday saying that Hurts asked the team's training staff to treat his calf on Oct. 8 after being cleated during a game against the Los Angeles Rams days earlier. An ultrasound was performed on Oct. 10 after the team flew to London. The results showed a superficial blood clot, but doctors and medical staff concluded "activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play."

The team says Hurts, who did not carry an injury designation before the game, played "without limitation" last weekend against the Jacksonville Jaguars and was able to practice fully Wednesday after receiving treatment earlier in the week.

A follow-up ultrasound was done Wednesday which "revealed movement in the small blood clot."

Hurts will miss Week 6 and there is currently no timetable for a return. The Eagles said they have been in communication with the NFL regarding the matter.

Tanner McKee, who has played six career NFL games since being drafted in 2023, will be the Eagles' starter.

articles.title: Patriots will reportedly activate receiver A.J. Brown from injured reserve after 4-game absence
articles.summary: Brown has been sidelined since suffering a high-ankle sprain during New England's season opener.
articles.body:
Receiver A.J. Brown is expected to play in the New England Patriots' Week 6 matchup with the New York Jets, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Brown, 29, has been sidelined since sustaining a high-ankle sprain in the Patriots' season opener versus the Seattle Seahawks. He left New England's 13-10 loss in the third quarter after catching three passes for 26 yards, and was placed on injured reserve the next day.

Going on IR meant that Brown would have to sit out for the next four games. Thus, he was eligible to be activated this week. Brown was a limited participant in all three of the Patriots' practice sessions for the week and is listed as questionable for Sunday .

Earlier in the week, head coach Mike Vrabel said "there is a chance" the veteran receiver would be able to return for Week 6.

"Whenever he'll be back, he should help us," Vrabel said on Monday during his weekly appearance on Boston's WEEI. "I hope that he's going to help us, but that remains to be seen yet when he'll be back. So we'll see how he does and move from there."

Brown's pending return looked like a strong possibility when the Patriots placed receiver Mack Hollins on IR prior to Week 5's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Before going on IR, Hollins had the most catches among Patriots wide receivers with 15 for 209 yards. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson and tight end Hunter Henry also have 15 receptions for New England (3-2).

The Patriots acquired Brown during the offseason from the Philadelphia Eagles, in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-round selection. Though he had 1,003 receiving yards last season with the Eagles (his lowest total in four seasons), Brown had reportedly grown frustrated with quarterback Jalen Hurts — and the Eagles' offense in general.

That led to Brown being traded before a three-year, $96 million extension kicked in that takes him through the 2029 season.

Brown is in his eighth NFL season, which began with the Tennessee Titans for three years. He was the team's second-round selection (No. 51 overall) out of Ole Miss.

The 6-foot-1 receiver was dealt to the Eagles during the 2022 NFL Draft for first- and fourth-round picks. He subsequently received a four-year, $100 million extension from Philadelphia.

A three-time Pro Bowler and two-time Second-Team All-Pro selection, Brown has 527 career receptions for 8,055 yards and 56 touchdowns.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Jim Harbaugh's Hot Seat and Chargers Trade Calls amid Justin Herbert, LA 0-5 Start
articles.summary: Despite the Los Angeles Chargers' 0-5 start to the season, head coach Jim Harbaugh's job is reportedly not in danger.
articles.body:
Despite the Los Angeles Chargers' 0-5 start to the season, head coach Jim Harbaugh's job is reportedly not in danger.

According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, Harbaugh "isn't going anywhere," and the Chargers aren't looking to sell off players either.

Pelissero added that Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz has told teams calling about potential trades that he is "not interested," as the Chargers are "holding out hope" that they'll be able to turn things around.

articles.title: “It connects my life and childhood to every single game”: How George Kittle’s father keeps him grounded with emotional letters before his important NFL games
articles.summary: George Kittle has plenty of reasons to get fired up before an NFL game.
articles.body: George Kittle has plenty of reasons to get fired up before an NFL game. But for the San Francisco 49ers tight end, one of his most personal pregame routines begins with a letter from his father, Bruce Kittle. The letters go beyond the usual words of encouragement. They connect George to his childhood, remind him of the person he was before NFL fame and help him prepare for the pressure that comes with playing at the highest level.The tradition began during George’s sophomore year at the University of Iowa and continued as his career took off. Before games, he reads his father’s words on the team bus and in the locker room. Over time, those notes grew into detailed stories that bring family memories, football lessons and even The Lord of the Rings into his preparation. How Bruce Kittle turns pregame letters into a personal ritualBruce does not simply tell his son to go out and play well. He thinks carefully about what George needs to hear before each game. In an Athletic report, Bruce explained that the letters reflect his view of how to help his son stay focused.“My letters are my vision of what George needs to hear to keep his head on straight,” Bruce said in the report. He also wants George to “keep his feet on the ground, make sure his ego is in check and be the guy he needs to be for his team.”That message takes on added weight as Kittle grows into one of the NFL’s most recognizable tight ends. The attention around him can be loud, but his father’s letters bring him back to the things that matter to his game: staying humble, trusting his preparation and putting the team first.His mother, Jan, also helps Bruce edit the letters. The notes include pictures, making them more personal than a standard motivational speech. George has described how the tradition has changed over the years.Kittle explained that the letters had evolved from “a pregame hype speech to a pregame story.” He added, “It connects my life and childhood to every single game.” A 12-page letter before the NFC Championship GameBruce’s letters can get remarkably detailed. Before the 49ers faced the Green Bay Packers in the NFC Championship Game on January 19, 2020, he wrote George a 12-page letter. Rather than relying only on football talk, Bruce drew on stories from “The Lord of the Rings”, using its battles and characters to frame the challenge ahead.He also worked NFL Next Gen Stats and analytics into his writing. The idea was to give George useful details while helping him picture the challenge in a way that made sense to him.Still, the letters were not simply about getting George fired up. Bruce wanted his son to stay calm when the stakes rose. As he explained in the same report, “To me, the bigger the stakes, the more stillness you need to really excel at a higher level.”That approach offers a glimpse into the preparation behind Kittle’s intensity on the field. Fans see the celebrations, physical blocks and big plays. Before kickoff, though, he also makes time for a quieter routine built around his father’s words.The letters cannot guarantee a win, but they give George something that statistics and game plans cannot provide on their own: a reminder of where he came from and the values he carries into every game.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dan Quinn Hot Seat, Josh Harris' Stance Updated in New NFL Rumors After Commanders' Tie vs. Giants
articles.summary: Despite the embarrassing moment for the Washington Commanders at the end of overtime last week resulting in a tie against the New York Giants, head coach Dan Quinn isn't in imminent danger of losing his job.
articles.body:
Despite the embarrassing moment for the Washington Commanders at the end of overtime last week resulting in a tie against the New York Giants, head coach Dan Quinn isn't in imminent danger of losing his job.

Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Commanders owner Josh Harris has "never been a believer in midseason coaching changes" and the expectation is Quinn will get the chance to turn things around starting on Monday night against the San Francisco 49ers:

"Commanders owner Josh Harris has never been a believer in midseason coaching changes. But in the wake of last week's overtime debacle in a tie with the Giants (which we talked about in depth on The Ringer NFL Show) he'll be paying close attention to how Dan Quinn's team responds Monday night at San Francisco."

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones added that Quinn, Jayden Daniels and offensive coordinator David Blough all addressed the team this week following the Giants' debacle to take accountability for the final sequence:

"Quinn spoke to the entire team Monday, telling them that everything starts with him and that he should have been better. The secondary message was that while everyone has to be accountable, everyone should hold others accountable, too. Daniels and Blough each addressed the offense individually."

articles.title: NFL rumors: Will Josh Jacobs start for Packers in potential Week 7 return?
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers are finally set to have Josh Jacobs back in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. The running back, who had been in the NFL Commissioner’s...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are finally set to have Josh Jacobs back in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. The running back, who had been in the NFL Commissioner's Exempt list to start the season due to a domestic violence arrest, will officially be removed from the list on Monday.

According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Jacobs is set to start immediately upon his return to the lineup against the Lions.

The Packers have gone 3-2 in their first five games of the season without Jacobs, and they have clearly missed the Pro Bowl running back's production. The Packers are comfortably in last place in rushing yards per game, averaging just 60.4. The Houston Texans, who are second from bottom, are averaging 19.4 rushing yards per game more.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

MarShawn Lloyd has proven to be ineffective during his time as the Packers' lead back. He has rushed for just 112 yards on 40 carries for a paltry 2.8 yards per rush. Second-year back Kaleb Johnson has not been much better with 106 yards on 27 carries. However, Lloyd did star with two touchdowns in the Packers' big 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears.

The lack of a reliable rushing attack has put a lot of pressure on Jordan Love, but the quarterback has been showing signs of improvement . After struggling with his accuracy to start the season, he has been more locked in of late. He's completed an impressive 47 out his last 61 pass attempts (77%) over the last two games.

Jacobs' return would be a major boost to Love and the Packers offense, especially in providing more of a threat in play action.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Injury Alert: A.J. Brown Expected to Play Week 6; Fantasy Fallout for Drake Maye and Patriots
articles.summary: A.J. Brown is expected back from IR. See how his return impacts the fantasy outlook for Drake Maye, Romeo Doubs, Hunter Henry, and Demario Douglas.
articles.body:
A.J. Brown's Impending Return Changes Fantasy Landscape in New England

Fantasy managers who invested heavily in the New England Patriots' passing game this offseason have spent the last month and a half navigating a turbulent landscape. When blockbuster offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the opening quarter of Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks, it felt like a cruel joke. Sidelined on Injured Reserve for the better part of two months, Brown left fantasy lineups scrambling and forced a heavy burden onto a patchwork receiving corps.

Now, according to reports from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the dark cloud is lifting. The Patriots are expected to activate Brown off Injured Reserve in time for their divisional matchup against the New York Jets. After returning to practice this week and testing his ankle, the star wideout is poised to reclaim his role as the undisputed fantasy stud wide receiver of this offense. While Brown may have a bit of a pitch count that limits his upside to more of a WR2 this week, his fantasy managers absolutely have to start him.

For fantasy football players, this news is an absolute earthquake. Inserting an elite, difference-making alpha back into an active offense changes the math across the entire roster. But how does this dramatic shift impact key offensive pieces like Drake Maye, Romeo Doubs, Hunter Henry, and Demario Douglas? Let's break down the fantasy fallout for Week 6.

For young quarterback Drake Maye, the return of his premier weapon provides an invaluable ceiling boost. Maye has experienced a bumpy start to the season while leaning on a patchwork receiving corps, but a route-running technician of Brown's caliber offers the ultimate safety valve and field-stretcher. With opposing defenses forced to dedicate heavy safety attention to Brown, Maye will benefit from wider throwing windows and softer underneath zones. While Maye has been one of the best fantasy quarterbacks over the last two weeks, his overall upside skyrockets now that he possesses a legitimate go-to option capable of turning simple plays into explosive gains. He has legit overall QB1 upside this week.

Romeo Doubs saw an expanded target share in Brown's absence, but the production has been erratic. With Brown drawing the primary cornerback coverage, Doubs slides back into a more natural secondary role. While he will face lighter defensive coverages, his total target volume will likely decrease, converting him into a high-upside, boom-or-bust flex play for Week 6.

Hunter Henry occupies a uniquely stable position amid this offensive reshuffle. Henry has quietly maintained reliable chemistry with Maye throughout the early weeks of the season, and Brown's presence on the perimeter should only help the veteran tight end. Elite wide receivers stretch defenses both vertically and laterally, opening up lucrative soft spots in the middle of the field where tight ends thrive. Henry retains his status as a steady back-end option, with his red-zone equity actually getting a boost because defenses can no longer focus solely on bracketing tight ends and slot receivers near the goal line. Consider Henry a high-end TE2 with TE1 upside this week.

WR Demario Douglas, New England Patriots

Meanwhile, Demario Douglas faces a more noticeable PPR floor dip. Douglas thrived on manufactured touches and short-area slot volume while the receiving room was decimated, but Brown's return eats directly into those underneath targets, turning Douglas into a game-script-dependent flex play or roster hold. Douglas belongs on the bench outside of deep fantasy leagues this week, and can be thrown back on the waiver wire in most leagues.

articles.title: NFL draft prospects 2027: Players to watch for Florida State vs. Miami
articles.summary: Ten 2027 NFL draft prospects to watch in today’s Florida State at Miami game. Will Darian Mensah be the first player off the board in the spring?
articles.body:
Week 7 of the college football season is here, and it brings a key Florida in-state rivalry game. The Florida State Seminoles head from Tallahassee to South Florida today to face the Miami Hurricanes.

This game obviously has plenty of meaning for our community, with so many people having attended or become fans of either team. It felt like the right time to bring in the Miami Dolphins' perspective and take a closer look at some of the 2027 NFL Draft prospects who could be on the field today.

The game kicks off at 7 p.m. Eastern on ESPN and Disney+.

Duce Robinson, wide receiver (Senior) – Robinson is a huge target – like a bigger-than-the-Dolphins-tight-ends huge target. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 230 pounds, Robinson uses his size to give his quarterback a receiver who will fight for contested passes in a huge catch radius. If he gets his hands on the ball, it is going to be a catch. He is not the most precise route runner, and he does not have the speed to pull away from anyone, so he relies on his size to make the catch rather than speed to create separation. He is probably a day-two prospect who can excel as a possession receiver and redzone target.

Charles Lester III, cornerback (Junior) – Lester is likely a developmental outside cornerback with good size. He is 6-foot-2 and 195 pounds, but he still needs to develop his technique, especially against faster, smaller wide receivers. He needs to clean up his work when receivers cut, but he can coach that up this year and in the NFL. He still has eligibility, so a 2027 return to college is not out of the question, but he could transition to the league, probably as a day-two pick. For Miami, where cornerback depth is a question mark, Lester could be an ideal option.

Ja'Bril Rawls, cornerback (Senior) – Another cornerback with good size (6-foot-1, 180 pounds), Rawls is behind his teammate in draft potential, but the potential for success in the NFL is there. He probably needs to add strength, and his frame suggests he can do that without sacrificing speed. He has the versatility to slide back to safety, which might be the better option. He is not the best tackler, and he will need to clean that up in the NFL, especially if he is expected to step up in run defense. A developmental defensive back option who should contribute on special teams, Rawls is likely a day-three prospect who could rise to the end of day two.

Quintrevion Wisner, running back (Senior) – The former Texas running back moved to Florida State this year after three seasons in Austin. He carried the ball 226 times for 1,064 yards in 2024, but he played only nine games in 2025 due to a hamstring injury. He has 29 carries for 141 yards this season, but is buried on the depth chart, and he has to prove he can be a receiving option out of the backfield before he can be considered a feature running back at the NFL level. He is a day-three depth running back option who can contribute on special teams.

Micahi Danzy, wide receiver (Redshirt sophomore) – Danzy is the smaller receiver on our FSU prospects list, but that is only because Robinson is ridiculously large. Danzy is listed at 6-foot-1 and 195 pounds, and he can line up in multiple roles among the receiving corps. He has track speed, setting the FSU school record in the 400, and started his college career as a running back. He has 19 receptions for 139 yards and two touchdowns this season. He uses his speed to his advantage but needs to keep building his route tree. He is probably a day-three prospect who could use his speed to battle his way into a day-two consideration.

Darian Mensah, quarterback (Redshirt junior) – Mensah is a modern college football player who bounces between teams; he started at Tulane, then spent a year at Duke before moving to Miami this year. He throws with anticipation and makes good decisions, but he does not always work through his progressions and still has to prove he can handle pressure. He does not have the strongest arm and throws great short-to-medium passes, but the ball can die on longer throws at times. He could be the first quarterback off the board this year, potentially as the number one overall pick.

Xavier Lucas, cornerback (Junior) – Lucas might be the ideal press-corner for the NFL. He has the size (6-foot-2, 200 pounds) to disrupt receivers at the line of scrimmage and the speed to keep up with the league's vertical threats. He contests passes well, using his size to break up jump balls, but he is more likely to knock the ball away than to come away with an interception. He is a liability on run defense, with seemingly no interest in getting his nose into the mess in front of him; he also needs to clean up his tackling. Lucas has missed the last month of the season with an undisclosed injury, but he is expected to return for tonight's game. He is probably a day-two prospect who is clearly not a finished product and will continue to grow in the NFL. For a Dolphins team in need of defensive secondary help, Lucas could be a key target.

Note: Lucas is the basis of the lawsuit from Wisconsin against Miami. Lucas played his freshman year at Wisconsin under a two-year Name, Image, and Likeness contract. He tried to transfer to Miami for his second season, but Wisconsin refused to enter him into the transfer portal, citing his contract. Lucas dropped out of Wisconsin and enrolled at Miami without entering the NCAA's transfer portal, and Wisconsin is alleging tampering by Miami to entice Lucas to transfer.

Damon Wilson II, edge (Senior) – The Dolphins will likely be highly interested in edge rushers in the 2027 Draft, and Wilson could put himself on the board. At 6-foot-4 and 250 pounds, Wilson has the size and athleticism needed to succeed in the NFL. He uses both speed and power to attack offensive tackles, but he needs to add counter moves to get off the block if his initial move does not win. He also needs to improve his edge-setting against the run. He has the flashes to be great in the NFL, but he hasn't shown the consistency yet. He broke out last year at Missouri with a nine-sack season, and he has tallied 3.5 sacks through the first five games this year, including 2.5 sacks against Clemson a couple of weeks ago. If he can keep up that production, he will be a second-round target who could slide into the end of the first round.

Samson Okunlola, offensive tackle/guard (Redshirt Junior) – Okunlola's potential is projected based on limited playing time at Miami. He did not get regular snaps until last year, when he rotated at left guard all season. He was clean, did not allow a sack, and showed he could be relied on in big spots. He slid out to left tackle this year, and he has been successful there as well – though he has had a penalty issue that needs to be cleaned up. He could bring that versatility to the NFL, allowing teams to use him as either a guard or tackle as needed. At 6-foot-6, 330 pounds, he still brings athleticism to the line and could be an effective mover to lead block in running situations. He is probably a day-two prospect who could start as a depth option at tackle and guard before settling into a starting role as a guard on the line.

Ryan Rodriguez, center (Redshirt Senior) – A sixth-year college player, Rodriguez has played both guard and center at Miami. He has had injury issues, including needing surgery in 2022 and 2024. He is 6-foot-2 and 300 pounds, which is smaller than most NFL interior linemen, but Miami's All-Pro center, Aaron Brewer, is 6-foot-2 and 290 pounds, so that might not be a major concern. He has to prove he can withstand the pressure of an entire season and anchor the line, but he has been instrumental in Miami's success early this year, especially given the turnover the Hurricanes had on the line from last year.

Honorable mention: Jamal Meriweather, tackle – The 6-foot-7, 305-pound Meriweather has a lot of potential and could be a good swing tackle in the NFL, but he has not gotten consistent playing time. He will get on the field at some point and is worth watching, but he is likely a late-round pick or undrafted free agent signing who can continue developing early in his NFL career.

articles.title: Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was listed as a possible trade target for the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Could DK Metcalf end up with the Indianapolis Colts? Recently, Aaron Zacharias of Horseshoe Heroes wrote about wide receivers the Colts need to consider before the NFL Trade Deadline passes. Metcalf, who's currently with the Pittsburgh Steelers , was on the list:

DK Metcalf is the least likely on this list for the Colts' future ambitions, but he's also the most interesting possible target. Either it's the Aaron Rodgers factor, or he's simply not a good fit with the Pittsburgh Steelers; Metcalf has, in any case, not worked out. There is a world where the Steelers could trade Metcalf after just one and a half seasons, or wait until they get a different quarterback next year. That said, if there is any interest in him from other teams, would the Steelers turn it away? The Colts could land a No. 1 target with actual No. 1 target experience."

Without a doubt, Indianapolis needs help at the wide receiver position. Does trading for DK Metcalf make sense?

Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts

The Seattle Seahawks drafted DK Metcalf in the second round (64th overall pick) of the 2019 NFL Draft. As a rookie, he caught 58 passes for 900 yards and seven touchdowns. He recorded seven receptions for 160 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles . It was the NFL record for most receiving yards by a rookie in a postseason game.

In 2020, Metcalf finished with 83 receptions for 1,303 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He also made the Pro Bowl and was named a second-team All-Pro.

Metcalf finished the 2023 campaign with 66 receptions for 1,114 yards and eight touchdowns. He was named to the second Pro Bowl of his career that year.

DK Metcalf was later traded to the Steelers in 2025. During his career in Pittsburgh, he has caught 78 passes for 1,075 yards and seven touchdowns.

Metcalf's production has been underwhelming this year. In five games, he has only recorded 19 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown on 37 targets.

The Colts wide receiver room is not elite by any stretch of the imagination. It wouldn't be great even if Alec Pierce was available.

Pierce is currently out with a heel injury, and is reportedly still a few weeks away from returning to the field. The former Cincinnati Bearcat signed a four-year, $114 million extension with the Colts during the offseason. Pierce was supposed to be "The Man" for Indy, but he has only played in two games this season.

Fellow Colts receivers like Josh Downs and newcomer Keenan Allen haven't stepped up in Pierce's absence. The team was rumored to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., but the Arizona Cardinals , of course, traded him to the Houston Texans instead.

Should Indy trade for DK Metcalf before this year's November 10 Trade Deadline? The Colts could use a two-time Pro Bowler like Metcalf. Yet, it's unclear what the team would have to give up in a deal. Plus, it's unclear whether the Steelers would even be willing to trade him.

Colts quarterback Daniel Jones would surely love to add DK Metcalf. What quarterback wouldn't want to add another offensive playmaker? Metcalf could team with tight end Tyler Warren and improve the team's pass-catching corps. But it's unlikely that such a trade will happen.

articles.title: Washington Commanders Rumor Offers MAJOR Update on What Gets Dan Quinn Fired in Week 6
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders better not have any notable mental lapses in Week 6, because a new rumor claims it is […]
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders better not have any notable mental lapses in Week 6, because a new rumor claims it is sure to cost Dan Quinn his job as head coach.

After Washington went 12-5 and reached the NFC Championship Game in the 2024 season, it seemed like the team had found the coach who could make them a consistent playoff contender. However, ever since, the Commanders have regressed.

Last season, they finished with a disappointing 5-12 record. Many chalked it up to injuries — specifically to quarterback Jayden Daniels. However, there were some worrisome signs during the 2025 campaign. It put added pressure on the coach to deliver better results in 2026. However, they are 1-3-1 heading into a Week 6 Monday Night Football clash against the San Francisco 49ers .

Their record is bad, but they seemingly hit a low point in the Quinn era last week when the offense completely lost track of how much time was left on the clock in overtime against the New York Giants and blew a chance at a game-winning field goal.

Washington Commanders would need to be blown out by San Francisco 49ers to fire Dan Quinn

It has only reignited the discourse about the 56-year-old's job security and the idea that he could be the first coach fired in-season. However, according to Tom Pelissero, while owner Josh Harris will be "paying close attention" on Monday night, he " has never been a believer in midseason coaching changes ."

That is why the NFL insider added that unless the Commanders suffer a blowout loss (very possible against a very good 49ers team) or there are obvious signs the team has quit on their coach, "expect Quinn to get the rest of the season to show he can get things turned in the right direction."

Furthermore, Daniels threw his support behind his coach after he mismanaged their final drive in Week 5, and the NFL insider claims, "Quinn has always had great command of the locker room."

articles.title: Chiefs need to stay on their toes against winless Chargers
articles.summary: Kansas City has an opportunity to end any hope for Los Angeles to turn this season around and they can’t overlook it.
articles.body:
It's hard to call a division matchup a trap game, but the (4-0) Kansas City Chiefs must avoid overlooking the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday afternoon.

According to Tom Pelissero, formerly of NFL Network , now with The Ringer and Netflix , the Chargers are "rejecting trade calls" because the team believes it is close to turning it around after an 0-5 start. There are no plans for "a fire sale."

That narrative could change if the Chiefs take care of business this weekend, but if Kansas City lets Los Angeles get its bounceback performance and pick up a win in the AFC West along the way, it could be the turning point the Chargers need to regroup.

Head coach Andy Reid understands the Chargers' desperation. A Reid-led Chiefs team once started 1-5 before ripping off enough consecutive wins to make the postseason in 2015.

During his press conference on Friday, Reid warned that Kansas City needs to stay alert and avoid getting caught off guard by an offensive mind looking to manufacture a win with a lengthy injury report .

"Well, you expect the unexpected," Reid said when asked about Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. "He's a sharp mind and very creative, so you've got to be on your toes. He does a nice job. (Chargers Head Coach) Jim (Harbaugh), likewise. I mean, you have two guys in there that are real good football guys, offensive minds."

Los Angeles will be without its two starting offensive tackles — Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater — along with its top wideout this year: Tre Harris. It's hard to know what the unit could look like with all the injuries, and the Chargers could play into the ambiguity to pull off a major upset.

With their season at a clear pivot point ahead of a Week 7 bye, Los Angeles will go all-out for a win in Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday. On offense, defense and special teams, the Chiefs must be prepared for anything, because the Chargers will play like they have nothing to lose.

articles.title: “He is ready to go”: Travis Kelce’s Kansas City Chiefs role take a significant turn as Dave Toub prepares him for an emergency position beyond tight end duties
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has another job to prepare for as the Kansas City Chiefs look to protect themselves against a special teams emergency.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has another job to prepare for as the Kansas City Chiefs look to protect themselves against a special teams emergency. The veteran tight end already carries a big workload on offense, but special teams coordinator Dave Toub wants him ready to step in at long snapper if the team needs him.The plan comes during a significant stretch of Kelce’s career. The 2026 season could be his last in the NFL, and the Chiefs are off to a 4-0 start. Currently, Kelce remains focused on his usual role. However, an injury to the team’s regular long snapper could put him in an unfamiliar position on game day.Dave Toub has a backup plan for Travis Kelce at long snapperToub recently explained why he wants Kelce ready to handle long-snapping duties if an emergency strikes. Speaking to reporters about the Chiefs’ backup options, the special teams coordinator said, “I definitely thought about it, and I said to myself, ‘We need to get Kelce.’”He added, “Because Kelce’s our guy. You can dial him up in two snaps, and he’s ready to go, but we need to practice it. The other guy that does it now is Gray, Noah Gray. So, two really good athletes that fit the bill.”The comments highlight Kansas City’s plan to prepare more than one player for a position that often goes unnoticed until something goes wrong. Long snappers handle the precise snaps required for punts and field goals. A poor snap can disrupt the entire play, leaving the holder, kicker and coverage unit scrambling to recover.The Chiefs currently rely on James Winchester as their regular long snapper. He has played every Kansas City game since joining the team in 2015, building a streak of 205 appearances, including playoff games, as of January 2026. The Chiefs re-signed him to a one-year, $1.75 million contract in March 2026. Chiefs have already faced a long-snapper emergencyKansas City has a reason to take this backup plan seriously. During a preseason game against the Detroit Lions in August 2024, Winchester left with a shoulder injury. Noah Gray stepped in to snap for punter Matt Araiza on Harrison Butker’s 56-yard field goal.Gray, a tight end, had never long-snapped in a game at any level. Kelce could not take over because he had already finished his day after the second offensive possession. Toub later praised Kelce’s ability and identified him as another backup option.The Chiefs’ concerns also echo a problem Jacksonville faced on October 12, 2026, against the Philadelphia Eagles. Jaguars long snapper Ross Matiscik injured his shoulder in the first quarter, forcing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton to take over. A high snap disrupted the timing on a late missed extra point, although Hamilton later snapped for Cam Little’s 57-yard game-winning field goal in Jacksonville’s 19-17 victory.That sequence showed how quickly a long-snapper injury can affect a game. Toub wants Kansas City’s emergency options to get practice before a similar situation arises.Kelce has already produced 246 receiving yards and two touchdowns through four games in the 2026 season, according to the supplied report. He finished 2025 with 76 catches for 851 yards.As of now, the Chiefs do not need Kelce to replace Winchester. But Toub wants him prepared if the situation changes.
